--- sidebar: daily-materials execute: freeze: true author: "Carmen Galaz García, Nathaniel Grimes" --- # $e^x$, Logs, and Lines Problem Set ::: {.callout-tip} ## Instructions Attempt each problem on your own before checking the [solutions](day3-problem-set-solutions.qmd). Feel free to work with anyone in the cohort after giving the problems a try! ::: ## $e^x$ and logarithms **1)** Forestry officials discover an invasion of an invasive insect in a county park. They estimate the insect population grows exponentially, following $N(t) = N_0 e^{rt}$, where $N_0$ is the initial number of egg masses counted per hectare, and $t$ is time in years since detection. At detection ($t=0$), officials count $N_0 = 150$ egg masses per hectare. Four years later, the count has grown to $400$ egg masses per hectare. a) Solve for the growth rate $r$. b) Forestry regulators will impose a mandatory quarantine zone if the population reaches $5{,}000$ egg masses per hectare. Using your value of $r$, solve for the time $t$ at which this threshold will be reached. c) State your answer to (b) as a full sentence. ## Lines and linear functions **2)** Find the equation of each of the following lines: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](day3-problem-set_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: **3)** A stream's water temperature increases as you move downstream from a shaded headwater spring. At a monitoring station 2 km downstream, the water temperature is 14°C. At a station 5 km downstream, the temperature is 20°C. Assume temperature increases linearly with distance downstream. a) Find the equation for water temperature $T$ (°C) as a function of distance downstream $x$ (km). b) Create a plot showing the line. Clearly label the axes, including units, and add a title. c) What is the $y$-intercept of this line, and what does it mean in the context of the stream? Answer in a full sentence.
**4)** A regional market for albacore tuna is described below, where $Q$ is quantity in thousands of pounds sold per week and $P$ is price in \$ per pound. (1) A fishery's weekly supply curve for tuna passes through $(Q,P) = (0, 20)$ and $(100, 70)$. Find the supply curve $S(Q)$ in slope-intercept form. (2) At a price of \$70/lb, weekly quantity demanded is 40 (thousand lbs); at \$20/lb, quantity demanded is 140 (thousand lbs). Find the inverse demand equation $D(Q)$. (3) Plot $S(Q)$ and $D(Q)$ on the same axes, with quantity on the $x$-axis and price on the $y$-axis. Label both axes clearly, including units. (4) Find the price and quantity at which supply equals demand and interpret this point in one sentence. --- *All the functions and example data are synthetic and were generated (some with the aid of Claude Code) for the purpose of this lesson.*
